summary.text: Atomic physics studies the atom as a system made of a nucleus and its electrons, usually treating each atom on its own.
Its focus is processes like excitation and ionization, where electrons absorb energy, jump between states, or are knocked out of the atom.
It is separate from nuclear physics, yet it supplies the underlying theory for plasma physics and atmospheric physics.

facts.label: Not nuclear physics
facts.value: Atomic physics studies nucleus plus electrons; nuclear physics studies the nucleus's reactions

facts.label: Binding energy
facts.value: The energy needed to remove an electron from its shell

facts.label: Ionization
facts.value: Happens when an electron absorbs more than its binding energy

facts.label: Periodic system
facts.value: Dmitri Mendeleev's table was a great step forward

facts.label: Modern boost
facts.value: Computing, lasers and detectors accelerated progress after World War II

items.prompt: A gas of atoms in a lamp bumps into each other only rarely. Why can physicists study each atom as if it were alone?

options.label: Atoms in a gas never interact with anything
Time between atom-atom contacts is huge compared with atomic processes
Gases contain only a single atom
Neighbouring atoms always cancel each other out

items.explain: In a gas or plasma the time-scales for atom-atom interactions are huge compared with the atomic processes, so each atom is in isolation most of the time.

items.prompt: An electron in an atom absorbs less energy than its binding energy. What happens?

options.label: It is ejected and the atom is ionized
It moves to an excited state

items.explain: Below the binding energy the electron moves to an excited state; only above it does the atom ionize.

items.prompt: An excited electron in a neutral atom drops to a lower state. What leaves the atom?

options.label: A photon carrying the energy difference

items.explain: Because energy is conserved, the atom emits a photon with the difference in energy.

items.prompt: A news article says atomic physics is the science behind nuclear bombs. What is the better distinction?

options.label: They are exactly the same field
Atoms are nucleus plus electrons; nuclei react

items.explain: The words are used interchangeably in everyday English, but physicists separate the atom as nucleus plus electrons from the study of nuclear reactions.

items.prompt: An atom absorbs a lot of energy in one of its innermost electrons, and an outer electron falls in to fill the gap. Which is a possible result?

options.label: The atom turns into a molecule

items.explain: The released energy can appear as a visible photon or characteristic X-ray, or go to another electron through the Auger effect.

items.prompt: Which field does atomic physics help explain, despite involving huge numbers of atoms?
items.explain: Since atoms act in isolation most of the time, atomic physics gives the underlying theory for plasma and atmospheric physics.
